scope: Observable main-chat contracts apply to every agent; missing evidence is a failure, never a policy exemption. Fixture evidence is not live/browser evidence.

derivation.method: main branch source, server test inventory, UX tests/browser suites, merge/commit subjects and loaded chat/release skills

policies.rule: Owner-scoped hermes-only: James explicitly requested 'Archimedes only' on 27 Oct 2026 for owned-open-work follow-through. Routed instructions, status projection and admissions remain untouched; this does not exempt any other chat feature.
Private agent history, memory and home are invisible to standard agents. Do not test against existing private agents; use fresh disposable synthetic data.
Agent model allowlists and restricted-provider unsupported combinations remain enforced; test an allowed model, never exempt the whole model picker.
An explicit files:none grant refuses attachments; files:own must support attached bytes. Do not count unavailable placement as policy.
Restricted runtime must use its per-agent Unix socket and edge transport; no host TCP fallback.

features.description: Provider loss rejects new sessions/runs only for already migrated agents, without affecting other runtime kinds
features.how_to_test: Use real Wizard HTTP for main, host-profile, legacy container and Unix restricted kinds. Admit a normal run with no provider app, then install a stopped capability and mark the synthetic container/restricted record as previously migrated. Assert 503 before upstream dispatch for marked agents; main/profile remain usable. Migration lifecycle is covered independently.

features.description: Owner-scoped Hermes-only owned follow-up processing without imposed style instructions; routed kinds retain done state and admission behavior.
features.how_to_test: Admit a synthetic HTTP turn per kind and inspect actual upstream instructions: no runtime receives OWNED_OPEN_WORK_INSTRUCTIONS, because reply and follow-up style belong to its persona. Project an owned Still open reply through the real session list, assert routed kinds stay done without owned_work or automatic sends, and execute the Hermes guard. tests/owned-open-work.test.ts additionally proves the main service's hidden continuation, restart dedupe and exact optional-handle behavior. These are disposable fixture checks, not live-model or browser proof.

features.description: A diagnosed expired sign-in waits for an observed unavailable-to-ready transition and resends the saved request once on the same locked model route.
features.how_to_test: Fail a real HTTP admission with a controlled zero-token sign-in error, observe unavailable then ready, and assert one same-model source-preserving resend on main, host-profile, container and restricted queues.

features.description: Every runtime receives the Supervisor spell and six Hermes session-injected tools; standard agents can report through their authenticated transport. Scheduled replies share Reporter validation.
features.how_to_test: Admit an ordinary run per kind; inspect shared spell, install asset bundle into disposable homes, call report through main loopback or per-agent credential/socket, check service-derived identity and queued review. Verify private/siloed refusal separately before ledger reads.
features.privacy_seal_exemption: Private and siloed agents refuse all Supervisor tools without sharing. Covered by tests/supervisor.test.ts and per-routed-kind refusal assertions; no standard runtime kind is exempt.

features.description: Reject self-identified agent-to-agent run/chat/steer writes into existing owner threads before runtime side effects; preserve ordinary sends.
features.how_to_test: For every runtime kind, POST agent-to-agent prefix and NOT-a-James-message inputs through run, steer, chat and chat/stream. Require HTTP 409 agent_to_agent_thread_write and no upstream writes, then accept a normal owner run and a Supervisor update that quotes the marker below its first line, and list sessions.

features.description: All agent kinds receive only Wizard OS facts, the persona pointer and the status protocol, never a reply-style rule, whatever response_style an older shell saved.
features.how_to_test: Admit fresh-install and legacy summary/concise/own turns through main, host-profile, container and restricted HTTP routes; assert settings read Own and actual upstream instructions contain Wizard facts, the persona pointer and STATUS_PROTOCOL_INSTRUCTIONS without reply-style rules. Fixture proof covers prompt delivery, not model compliance.

features.description: The optional signed Android companion preserves each routed reply while asynchronously stopping and parking its native recording.
features.how_to_test: In wizard-ux run node --test tests/shell-recording-routes.test.mjs. The real parkReply function runs for main, host-profile, container and restricted routes with asynchronous shell and synchronous full-app recorders; it preserves session, agent, typed draft and audio, and acknowledges only after durable held custody. Meeting cancellation also awaits native bytes before acknowledgement. This is synthetic source-executed evidence, not live provider or physical-phone proof. Companion UX PR: humanitylabs-org/wizard-ux#504.

features.description: Agent-owned thread collections persist independently of agent runtime kind and hydrate all visible members outside global archive windows
features.how_to_test: Authenticate as each main/host-profile/container/restricted agent (restricted via its Unix gateway), list/search/create/add/remove/delete own Spaces (spaces_add and full PUT snapshots keep a chat in one Space per agent), refuse foreign Spaces as not_found, project assistant-only subject metadata, file by status-line space, restart and verify durable membership. Managed-container startup upgrades are covered in tests/managed-harness-upgrade.test.ts. In wizard-ux, qa-chats-focus.cjs pickerAcceptance verifies main and routed New Space fills use the scoped Spaces tool instruction (never a main-only CLI), exactly once through the normal outbox with the selected agent. In wizard-ux, node --test tests/space-members.test.mjs checks missing-member hydration for main, host-profile, container and restricted routes, scope changes, hidden/private discovery, 500 members and bounded polling. QA_SPACE_MEMBERS_ONLY=1 node qa-chats-focus.cjs <origin> verifies phone/desktop Focus shows 82 visible members with 62 archived beyond the global archive-50, keeps All windowed and preserves Back. These are fixture/browser checks, not live runtime proof.

features.description: Each agent learns which of its own apps does which job, and the main agent's pointer skills send it through the app's shipped skill first.
features.how_to_test: Install a synthetic app with a provides job and a shipped skill into the real Service's apps.json, restart, and open the wizard MCP gateway with each kind's own credential and transport. Main: the wizard-job-<job> pointer skill is written, tells it to load the app's skill with skill_view first, and the gateway kernel points at that skills index. Other kinds have no pointer skills: their gateway kernel lists the job -> app map for their own apps instead. Uninstall: the pointer disappears and no kind is told about the app. Disposable fixture checks; the live-model proof for the main agent is ops/acceptance/pointer-skills (fresh KVM VM).

features.description: Stop shows the moment a message is sent; before the run exists it withdraws the pending send (no run admitted), after that it stops the exact run from the receipt
features.how_to_test: In wizard-ux run node --test tests/stop-before-run.test.mjs. The real outbox runs against a local HTTP boundary: Stop during upload, server transcription or offline waiting creates zero /v1/runs calls and keeps the recording; Stop while the run POST is in flight resolves with the receipt's run id; a steer in flight that is rejected after Stop never becomes a new turn. The real LIVE.cancelSend block runs for main, host-profile, container and restricted threads and withdraws only that thread's sends and stops only its own run (including a reply queued to steer the live run, and a slow phone take arriving after the tap hold). This is synthetic source-executed evidence; fenced browser QA on a scratch shell is reported separately. Companion UX PR: humanitylabs-org/wizard-ux#649.

features.description: Pinned Chats threads are the same on every device of the owner for main and routed threads; a stale or simultaneous device never drops or revives another device's pin.
features.how_to_test: In wizard-ux run node --test tests/chat-pins.test.mjs: pins key on the rendered row id for main, host-profile, container and restricted threads; a pin on one client shows on another and an unpin syncs back; a client that has not pulled keeps the other's pin; GET,GET,PUT,PUT between two clients keeps both pins (read-back replay); offline taps stay queued. Synthetic source-executed evidence; live two-browser check recorded on humanitylabs-org/wizard-ux#670.

features.description: Shared Chats lists (Spaces and their members, subject order, pins) keep every device's and agent's change for main and routed threads: edits are item operations applied atomically by the service, never a device's whole cached list, so a stale or simultaneous device cannot drop another's edit.
features.how_to_test: In wizard-agent-service, npx vitest run tests/ui-preferences.test.ts covers PATCH item operations (concurrent devices on one list, idempotency, gone Space no-op, 400 without writing, PUT kept for older shells). In wizard-ux, node --test tests/synced-lists.test.mjs runs every synced list key through tests/two-devices.mjs (stale device and GET,GET,PUT,PUT race, with and without PATCH support) for main, host-profile, container and restricted thread ids. Synthetic source-executed evidence; live two-browser check recorded on the wizard-ux PR.
